rv.q: It is a work of considerable intelligence and emotional force—one that grips, disturbs, and compels in equal measure.
Peter Coleman’s take on Joseph Goebbels, one of history’s most horrifying characters, is quite forgettable.

cn.t: James Clements' "Beauty Freak" delivers a bracing, intricately wrought examination of Leni Riefenstahl that anatomizes history with glittering precision, exploring the seductions of artistic genius and the moral complexities of fascism's rise.
